title: Project: sensor log statistics
lesson:
Microcontrollers log readings, and something has to make sense of them. You'll write the program that reads a sensor log and reports on it, the same job a weather station, a tank monitor or a soil sensor needs.

The input is one reading per line (a temperature, say), until the input ends:

```
21.5
24.0
31.2
```

Your program reads them all with `while (scanf("%lf", &x) == 1)` and keeps running totals as it goes, so it never needs to store the whole log (important on a board with 2 KB of memory):

- the **count**, **minimum**, **maximum** and **average**;
- the number of **alarms**: readings above 30.0.

Then print exactly:

```
count 3
min 21.5
max 31.2
average 25.6
alarms 1
```

(one decimal place on the numbers). If there are no readings at all, print just `no readings`.

Tips: start min and max from the **first** reading, not from 0. Keep the total as a `double`. This is the same pattern as Arduino's ino-csvlog block and the Python course's data units, so you'll see it again in every language.

exercises.title: Sensor report
exercises.prompt: Read readings until the input ends and print count, min, max, average (1 decimal place) and alarms (readings above 30.0), as in the lesson. With no readings print: no readings

tests.name: all below zero
tests.hint_if_fail: Start min and max from the first reading, not 0.

hints: Keep count, total, min, max, alarms. On the first reading (count == 0) set min and max to it.
After the loop: if (count == 0) { printf("no readings\n"); return 0; }

quiz.q: Why keep running totals instead of storing every reading?
choices: Tiny boards have very little memory, and the log can be any length
quiz.why: Constant memory, any length of log.

quiz.q: Why start min from the first reading?
choices: Starting at 0 breaks when every reading is negative (or positive, for min)

quiz.why: It returns how many it read; EOF (-1) at the end.

explain: Explain project: sensor log statistics to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
